question: Can a deliberately constrained neural architecture fit hyperelastic data while selecting an interpretable constitutive law and satisfying mechanics requirements by construction?

key_findings.claim: CANN maps deformation invariants to a scalar free energy, differentiates that energy to obtain stress, and restricts connectivity, activations, and nonnegative weights to encode objectivity, incompressibility, thermodynamic consistency, growth behavior, and a sufficient polyconvex form.
key_findings.evidence: Sections 3 and 5 derive invariant inputs and stress from the free-energy gradient. The example network separately sums functions of I1 and I2, uses linear/quadratic/exponential atoms, forces nonnegative weights during Adam optimization, and omits mixed invariant terms.

key_findings.claim: The eight-term incompressible isotropic model contains several familiar rubber laws as exact sparse submodels, making selected weights interpretable as moduli and exponential coefficients.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 26-32 explicitly recover neo-Hookean, Blatz-Ko, Mooney-Rivlin, Yeoh, Demiray, nearly incompressible, and Holzapfel-style terms by zeroing all but selected paths and algebraically mapping path products to physical parameters.

key_findings.claim: On legacy rubber stress-stretch tables, CANN fits sparse single-mode data smoothly outside the observed range and selects a small subset of atoms, while a tanh network can oscillate or flatten.
key_findings.evidence: Six uniaxial datasets are fit with a 12-weight CANN; plotted errors become visually negligible after under 10,000 epochs and extrapolated curves remain smooth. The fully connected baseline uses 16 weights plus nine biases and exhibits sparse-data oscillation and abrupt out-of-range flattening.

key_findings.claim: Richer multi-mode data reduces parameter non-identifiability in the demonstrations, but the paper does not establish uniqueness or predictive validity beyond a few initializations and one material family.
key_findings.evidence: Uniaxial-only fits reach equally good curves with different active atoms across six initializations. Simultaneous uniaxial, equibiaxial, and pure-shear fits repeatedly produce one reported three-term model at each temperature, at the cost of small systematic fit errors; there is no formal identifiability theorem or held-out multiaxial experiment.

method.core_idea: Turn a curated library of mechanically admissible energy atoms into a sparse, differentiable network so fitting weights performs both constitutive-model selection and calibration.
method.mechanism: Preprocessing computes objective invariants, selected nonmixing paths apply polynomial and exponential atoms, nonnegative outputs sum to free energy, automatic differentiation returns Piola stress, and mean-squared stress error trains the atom weights.
assumptions: The material is hyperelastic and history independent; the main demonstration is isotropic and perfectly incompressible.
The chosen invariant and activation library contains an adequate constitutive response.
Nonnegative separable atom sums provide an acceptable sufficient polyconvex family.
Homogeneous stress-stretch measurements are rich enough to identify the desired law.

techniques.role: Guarantees stress derives from a scalar stored-energy function.
Hardwires frame indifference and selected material symmetries.
Makes sparse paths correspond to named classical model terms.
Imposes monotonicity and a sufficient convexity structure while preventing arbitrary mixed terms.

evaluations.setting: Six historical uniaxial rubber/foam datasets with as few as seven points
evaluations.metric: stress-curve fit, qualitative extrapolation, active paths, and loss reduction
evaluations.result: CANN achieves smooth sparse fits and four-order loss reduction; active terms are not unique under uniaxial data alone.
evaluations.baseline: Fully connected tanh networks of several depths and widths.

evaluations.setting: Rubber at 20 and 50 degrees under uniaxial, equibiaxial, and pure-shear modes
evaluations.metric: simultaneous curve fit and repeatability over initialization
evaluations.result: Multi-mode training selects a repeated three-term energy and explicit physical parameters, with visible under/over-estimation in stiffening regions.
evaluations.baseline: Separate single-mode CANN fits and classical named rubber models represented within the library.

limitations: The demonstrations cover homogeneous, isotropic, incompressible, history-independent rubber response rather than finite-element boundary-value tests or complex paths.
The atom library creates interpretability by construction but cannot discover physics outside its predefined functional vocabulary.
Uniqueness is inferred from a handful of restarts, not proved or tested under noise and experimental uncertainty.
Extrapolation quality is judged visually without held-out measurements outside the training stretch range.
A restrictive sufficient polyconvex form can exclude admissible or practically important material responses.
failure_modes: Sparse loading modes leave I1 and I2 contributions non-identifiable despite an excellent stress fit.
All library atoms are misspecified, producing a stable but biased constitutive law.
Polyconvex restrictions over-regularize responses involving microstructural instabilities or nonconvex effective behavior.
Noise activates spurious atoms because exact zeros are not explicitly selected by a sparsity penalty.
A good homogeneous calibration becomes inaccurate or unstable inside a finite-element simulation.
reusable_insights: Model discovery is only identifiable relative to both a candidate library and an excitation design.
Enforcing stress as an energy derivative is stronger and easier to audit than penalizing thermodynamic residuals after prediction.
Report active-term stability across bootstrap samples, not only optimizer restarts.
Validate learned constitutive laws on held-out loading paths and boundary-value simulations.
open_questions: What loading modes are minimally sufficient to identify each invariant contribution under realistic noise?
How should the atom library expand to anisotropy, compressibility, viscoelasticity, plasticity, and damage without losing auditability?
Can Bayesian or sparse-selection uncertainty distinguish multiple equally plausible constitutive laws?
When does enforced polyconvexity improve simulation robustness versus impose harmful approximation bias?

competitive_landscape.title: Thermodynamics-based Artificial Neural Networks for constitutive modeling
competitive_landscape.difference: TANN hardwires free-energy and dissipation relations for inelastic material-point histories. CANN focuses on hyperelastic model selection with human-readable atom weights and adds explicit objectivity/polyconvex structure.

competitive_landscape.title: Polyconvex anisotropic hyperelasticity with neural networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Klein et al. use input-convex networks and group/invariant constructions on challenging anisotropic metamaterial data and test broader deformations. CANN is less expressive but maps paths directly to classical laws and parameters.

competitive_landscape.title: Data-driven Tissue Mechanics with Polyconvex Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
competitive_landscape.difference: Tac et al. use monotone neural ODEs for flexible polyconvex invariant derivatives and include skin data and finite-element simulations. CANN supplies simpler closed-form atom selection but less extensive downstream validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural networks meet hyperelasticity: A guide to enforcing physics
competitive_landscape.difference: Linden et al. systematically handle compressibility, stress/energy normalization, growth conditions, noisy data, and finite-element use. It broadens and audits physics constraints beyond the reviewed paper's incompressible rubber prototype.

competitive_landscape.title: Input convex neural networks: universal approximation theorem and implementation for isotropic polyconvex hyperelastic energies
competitive_landscape.difference: Geuken et al. prove universal approximation within the isotropic polyconvex class using signed singular-value polynomials. CANN offers no comparable completeness theorem and deliberately searches a much smaller interpretable library.

competitive_landscape.title: On limitations of polyconvexity
competitive_landscape.difference: Klein et al. show analytically and empirically that polyconvex neural constitutive models can be too restrictive for some homogenized microstructures. This qualifies CANN's implication that stronger hard constraints are uniformly beneficial.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after current primary-source comparison: CANN's strongest distinct contribution is a transparent constitutive-atom network whose sparse paths recover named laws and physical parameters while honoring a useful set of hard constraints. It is not unrestricted automated discovery, and later work supplies stronger expressivity theory, compressible formulations, finite-element validation, and evidence that polyconvexity can itself be a limiting bias.
reviewer_notes: Reviewed all 31 pages, including mechanics derivations, architecture and activation design, optimizer constraints, benchmark tables, every fit, initialization audit, extracted parameter values, and discussion. Six prior, concurrent, and subsequent primary arXiv sources were checked on 2026-08-23.
